sources.citation: Link, Christa. 1978. Units in Wobe discourse. In Joseph E. Grimes (ed.), Papers on discourse (SIL Publications in Linguistics 51), 226-236. Dallas: SIL.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p.226 footnote gives phonemes and syllable patterns (V, CV, CVV, CcV, CcVV) and: 'Tone has not been written in this paper, not because it is considered unimportant, but because it does not appear to affect the phenomena described here and because it is only partly analyzed. In fact, Wobe has a four-level tone system with glides, used to indicate both lexical and grammatical distinctions.' Fieldwork Kouibly near Man from 1972.

sources.citation: Bôle-Richard, Rémy. 2006. Unité et diversité du wɛ de Côte d'Ivoire. Journal of West African Languages 33(2): 109-142.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Comparative segmental and tonal phonology of Guéré / Wobè (Gbeon, Kouibly; also a Fakobly Wobè lect) / Nidrou; sec. 4.2 (p.129) Wobè has 9(+2) tonemes, 9 melodic contours on monosyllables and 15 on disyllables; 'accent' occurs only for tone diacritics (p.116, p.125).

sources.citation: Singler, John Victor. 1984. On the underlying representation of contour tones in Wobe. Studies in African Linguistics 15(1): 59-75. doi:10.32473/sal.v15i1.107520
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Reanalysis of Bearth & Link's tone data with four level tones and autosegmental association (p.59 abstract; p.60 feature chart); no mention of stress, accent or prominence.

sources.citation: Bearth, Thomas & Christa Link. 1980. The tone puzzle of Wobe. Studies in African Linguistics 11(2): 147-207.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Tao dialect (Kouibly area). p.148: syllable structure C1(C2)V1(V2)(V3), 14 contrastive tones on CV monosyllables, 'We will tentatively take the vowel as the unit of tone placement'; sections on tone distribution, F0 realization (mingograms) and morphotonology. The words stress/accent/prominence never occur in a prosodic sense (a full-text search for stress/accent the text layer: 'stress' only as a verb, pp. 165, 171).

sources.citation: Hofer, Verena. 1978. Types et séquences de propositions en wobé. In Joseph E. Grimes (ed.), Papers on discourse (SIL Publications in Linguistics 51), 323-334. Dallas: SIL.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on accent. p.324 footnote: phoneme list; nasalisation 's'étend sur le mot phonologique entier'; 'Il y a quatre tons ponctuels: 1 haut, 2 mi-haut, 3 mi-bas, 4 bas, et plusieurs tons modulés. L'étude de la phonologie et du ton n'est pas encore complétée.' Syllable structures V, CV, CVV, CcV, CcVV.

sources.note: The only full grammar of Wobé; its phonology chapter is the most likely place for a statement on accent/stress (or its absence). The PDF exists on sil.org (archive record 3367, 49.88 MB) but the site's an automated-access block blocks our network and no archived copy at the Internet Archive exists; a browser download or a library scan (the Harvard library catalogue) would settle it.
